description: Everything the main window may do: the core permissions only. The UI reaches the Rust core through the app's own commands (dispatch, subscribe_events, core_state, doc_open, doc_import, doc_export, doc_close, open_external, lock, unlock, backup_export, backup_import, attachment_write, attachment_read, attachment_import_path, attachment_import_url, attachment_save_as, attachment_open, export_run, import_run, save_text_file, backup_folder_choose, backup_run_now, ai_status, ai_endpoint_set, ai_generate, ai_chat, ai_cancel, ai_search, ai_transcribe, mcp_status, mcp_client_grants_set, shell_events_subscribe, shell_labels_set, menu_bar_show, menu_bar_hide, presence_send, presence_events, dictation_status, dictation_select, dictation_install, dictation_install_cancel, dictation_import, dictation_remove, dictation_start, dictation_audio, dictation_stop, dictation_cancel, drive_status, drive_connect, drive_disconnect, drive_client_set, drive_backups_list, drive_backup_download, drive_cancel, backup_folder_list), which need no permission entries. There are no filesystem, shell, dialog, opener, notification, deep-link, single-instance, tray, menu or global-shortcut permissions: the webview cannot call tauri-plugin-opener, tauri-plugin-dialog, tauri-plugin-notification, tauri-plugin-deep-link or tauri-plugin-global-shortcut itself (the shell's Rust code shows the OS notification of a due reminder, from the reminders' timer, with no permission). open_external hands the system only http, https and mailto links; the backup, attachment, export, import and save_text_file commands open the native file dialogs from Rust (the webview never passes a path), the dispatch command refuses a SettingsSet of the settings only the shell writes (app.backup.folder, app.backup.last, app.backup.drive, app.ai.endpoint) and the requests only the shell makes (AiIndexNext, AiIndexStore, McpCall, McpClientGrantsSet), attachment_import_url downloads one image from an https link on the person's explicit action (the webview loads no remote content), the ai_* commands make every call to Ollama from Rust (the webview's CSP still allows no network), ai_endpoint_set and mcp_client_grants_set ask for consent in a native dialog made from Rust, the MCP server listens on 127.0.0.1 only from the shell, shell_events_subscribe only receives what the shell sends the page on its own account: the atomik-kb://page/<uuid>[#<uuid>] links the OS hands the app (the shell registers the scheme, reads the link the app was started with and forwards a second launch, all from Rust; the shell ignores anything else and logs no link), the quick capture, the tray's lock and the state of the capture shortcut (the shell builds the tray icon and registers the global shortcut from Rust, so the webview's capability gains nothing for either), and shell_labels_set only changes the words of the tray menu and the menu bar (1 to 64 characters each, never logged), and menu_bar_show and menu_bar_hide only show or hide the native menu bar, which the shell builds from Rust (the webview's capability gains nothing for it; the UI sends menu_bar_show for a lone Alt press and the menu's choices reach the page as shell_events_subscribe messages), and attachment_open writes a private copy under the app cache directory and hands it to the system opener from Rust, which needs no permission, and presence_send and presence_events only move presence frames that the core seals and opens (the webview holds no key; frames go through the shell's own socket to the configured sync server, and the webview's CSP still allows no network). The dictation_* commands (ADR-0053) need no permission either: dictation_install shows a native consent dialog made from Rust before it downloads a speech model (the webview's CSP still allows no network and it never passes a path), dictation_import opens a native folder dialog from Rust, the recognizer runs in a separate sidecar process (kb-speech) that only the shell's Rust code starts, dictation_audio only moves the samples a session is given, the person's audio is held in memory and never stored, and nothing a person says is logged. The drive_* commands and backup_folder_list (ADR-0059) need no permission either: drive_connect shows a native consent notice made from Rust and then opens the Google sign-in in the system browser from Rust, the loopback address that receives its answer is bound to 127.0.0.1 only by the shell and checks the Host header, the refresh token lives in the OS keystore and the access token in memory only (the webview holds neither and its CSP still allows no network), every request to Google is made from Rust over HTTPS, the dispatch command refuses a SettingsSet of app.backup.drive, drive_backup_download writes a staging file under the app data directory that the page can only hand to backup_import, and backup_folder_list opens a native folder dialog from Rust and lists the names, sizes and times of the .atomikkb files of one folder.
